# R5e6506510f: Easy-spiral full-recipe counterexample (e7c9af9862207fd6bd921d6d10a2d1a0d26751e6)
# Easy-Spiral Full-Recipe Counterexample

## Sources and Definitions
Read q_6b5bfc, K1020/K1015/K1061/K1066, R1dd74ea5c0 and existing K1097/K1099. Frozen initial inputs: 953 history records, 64 claims, 11527 allowed-lab candidates. Checkpoint refresh pinned J6d7669e1b45e_research_e0003; initial sources remain archived. Only allowed lab datasets were trained.

History gives ordinal gold, not CE margins. Depth denotes hidden blocks after the input projection. LN acts before each block Linear; residual addition precedes activation. Delta=lr*T is a nominal proxy, not actual AdamW displacement. CE is held-out test cross-entropy, lower better.

## Historical Counterexample
q_6b5bfc: one turn, point seed125762377, train1024/test2048, T2048,bs16, default Linear initialization; shared AdamW(.9,.999),lr.0003,wd1e-5. Gold D<A<B<E<C, whereas prediction B<E<D<C<A failed.

D=d3w48 plain LeakyReLU(.01),LN[F,T,F]; A=d3w48 plain SiLU,LN[T,F,F]; B=d2w48 residual LeakyReLU,LN[T,T]; E=d2w48 residual LeakyReLU,LN[T,F]; C=d1w64 residual GELU,LN[T].

D/B holds width, activation and complete training recipe constant but bundles depth, skips and LN count/position. D/A bundles activation and LN position. C changes width, activation and depth. Historical numerical margins are unavailable.

K1061’s SGD,Delta<.1,depth>=4 plain scope does not cover this case. K1066’s deeper-residual/more-LN preference does not rank these rivals. K1020 and K1015 already reject universal LN/residual total orders.

## Comment Audit
Exclude target q and restrict prior epochs<4, easy=1–1.5 turns. Shared optimizer type/lr/T, deeper plain versus shallower residual, equal positive LN count, adaptive optimizers reconstructs **7/9 across six questions; Delta>=.5 is2/2**.

Pairs (plain/residual, plain win): q_b94d5a E/B yes; q_03cc9f B/A no; q_56e62b C/A yes,E/A yes,D/A no; q_b9a1d3 A/D yes; q_1fb83b E/B yes; q_99babc C/D yes,E/D yes.

Qualification: q_b94d5a uses Adam decay0 versus.001. Exact optimizer/budget matching removes it: **6/8, high-Delta1/1**. Thus 2/2 is not exact-recipe evidence. Including equal zero-LN adds q_0d5731, a plain win; including SGD changes counts again. Broad prior easy type/lr/T audit is9/13, high3/5, including two losses in q_0a7f2f.

The reconstructed nine pairs have only two equal-width and two equal-activation pairs; none match both. All LN masks and recipes are archived. Counts sharing candidates are not independent replications.

## Preregistration and Method
Published the initial R5e6506510f version at `11bde9d909e0760585959e892f6200c3055e4aaf` before valid experiments. Selected allowed one-turn splits05d021/06bcc2 without target-recipe outcomes. Primary prediction D<B on both; secondary prediction full gold transfers. Exploratory prediction D beats terminal-LN plain was marked uncertain.

Existing K1097/K1099 runs use lr3e-5,wd0,T1024,width192/256,terminalLN and were not repeated. No persisted requested d3w48 plain FTF run existed.

Ran D/A/B/E/C plus Leaky plain d3w48 TFF and FFT, residual d3w48 FTF, and plain d2w48 TT. Same optimizer/default init/budget/loss; width48 except historical C64. Measurement sets: `exp:25d081c4fa1f` and `exp:596e2d453da7`.

All18 variants returned finite mean/SD and error=null;180 seeds were scheduled under the tool’s ten-seed protocol. Returned rows lack failed_seeds/excluded and individual-seed counts, so zero failures and an uncensored ten-seed denominator cannot independently be certified. No invalid condition was silently dropped; these are tool-reported ten-seed summaries with a failure-audit limitation.

## Results
CE mean ± SD:

| Variant | 05d021 | 06bcc2 |
|---|---:|---:|
|D|.000074171 ± .000014811|.000066597 ± .000013096|
|A|.000388582 ± .000245302|.000310086 ± .000165995|
|B|.000602241 ± .000155156|.000540049 ± .000111490|
|E|.001110694 ± .000285313|.000962867 ± .000261619|
|C|.006403003 ± .001135196|.005675879 ± .000983619|
|plain d3 Leaky TFF|.000220759 ± .000039852|.000198777 ± .000042048|
|plain d3 Leaky FFT|.000103414 ± .000026862|.000114403 ± .000028519|
|residual d3 Leaky FTF|.000402686 ± .000093255|.000347508 ± .000066145|
|plain d2 Leaky TT|.000292506 ± .000033858|.000286894 ± .000031194|

**D/B ratios .123157/.123316; B-D margins .000528071/.000473452. Full D<A<B<E<C transfers2/2.**

Fixed d3/mask/activation residual/plain ratios5.429/5.218; fixed d2 TT ratios2.059/1.882. Skips worsen endpoint CE in these cells. Plain middle-LN/terminal-LN ratios.717/.582; first-LN/middle-LN2.976/2.985.

At d3 TFF, SiLU/Leaky ratios1.760/1.560. Activation and LN-position controls both supply comparisons consistent with D<A. B/E=.542/.561: terminal LN helps residual d2, while middle rather than terminal LN wins for plain d3. Neither LN count nor an unnormalized-tail penalty total-orders these recipes.

## Uncertainty, Failed Transfer and Alternatives
SDs are seed spread, not paired intervals; covariance, raw seeds and trajectories are unavailable. A’s spread is substantial. Large CE ratios coexist with absolute margins below.001. Endpoint means do not establish optimization dynamics or a causal mechanism.

No primary or full-order transfer failed on these two splits. Failed broader extrapolation remains: R1dd74ea5c0/K1099 predicted stronger matched deep/shallow benefit on harder data, but fixed-width/SiLU d5res/d3plain favored deep on all four splits and proportionally more on easy (.685/.673 versus.864/.882). Its easy d5 skip/plain ratios1.099/1.230 cannot be pooled with present d3 effects.

Historical q_03cc9f and q_56e62b D/A oppose deeper-plain preference; q_0a7f2f supplies high-Delta SGD losses. Easy data and unnormalized tails do not guarantee plain dominance.

Competing accounts include nonlinear composition depth, skip-conditioned optimization, LN placement/feature scaling, activation-conditioned fitting and seed-tail behavior. Controls distinguish endpoint effects, not mediation. Two existing easy splits are not a random population sample.

Unmeasured predictions: a third allowed one-turn split at this exact recipe should preserve D<B and D<A; reversal rejects transfer. Changing only rate to3e-5 or budget to1024 is predicted to weaken D/B advantage, but remains untested. Seed-resolved paired training and trajectories would distinguish systematic effects from rare-seed failures.

The original q split was not regenerated. Lab LeakyReLU slope is null/default in returned schema, not independently certified. Original-question margins, explicit slope control, audited failures and paired uncertainty remain unresolved. No causal turns statement is supported: seed and coordinate scale change across existing datasets.

## Reproducibility and Publication
`easy_spiral/` contains frozen history/KB/lab, extracted pair tables, all18 experiment rows, `report.md` and `analyze.py`. Reproduction assertions passed. Published **R5e6506510f**, commit `ceea32dbbd22c1504b5aac24c87c44ee92f3e900`. Added exactly one scoped 538-character claim, **K1105**; no parent rewrites. This is independently reviewable empirical evidence, not a finished theory.

# Rc66dd0caab: Equal-LN spiral boundary: final panel, uncertainty and prospective counterexamples (1ab541d5fbcf8e80c73c885f4d49dc80c726bb3a)
# Equal-LN Spiral Boundary: High-Rate Architecture Audit

Published as **Rc66dd0caab**, commit `90965406de2c8e7ea71f16932f59d4bd220cd431`. Reproducible inputs, measurements, analysis and full report are committed.

## Question And Sources

Can residual/depth comparisons be predicted at equal LN without counting normalizers?

Frozen history and KB were read before experiments and saved in `inputs/history.json` and `inputs/kb.json`; allowed lab entries are in `inputs/lab.json`. Focal misses were q_457ab7, q_79695d, q_07bc60 and q_3e4d33. Their gold rankings do not isolate feature scale, optimizer dynamics or radius retention.

K1066 retains its **strictly MORE-LN, shared optimizer/lr/T** scope. K1120/K1123 describe mixed RMSprop-versus-Adam recipes, not a shallow-over-deep rule; q_3e4d33’s same-RMS reversal warns against that transfer. K1097/K1099’s low-rate controls were not repeated. K1112 used Leaky slope .1, not original .01.

## Methods And Preregistration

Use q_07bc60’s exact optimizer/schedule: **AdamW lr .003, betas (.9,.999), decay .0001, T256, batch16, default initialization, cross entropy**.

Fix width192/ReLU; cross depth2/4, residual off/on, and first-only versus terminal-only preLN. Every cell has **exactly one LN**. Residual comparisons fix depth, width, activation and LNmask. Depth comparisons preserve LN count but necessarily change parameter count. Depth excludes input/head projections.

Primary easy splits were one-turn `05d021/06bcc2`; hard splits were two-turn `016ff9/01793b`. Each has 1024 train and 2048 test points. Ten seeds0–9 were used per cell.

The initial report was published before training. Preregistered predictions: residual helps everywhere; d4 hurts easy and helps hard; terminal LN beats first LN everywhere. These predictions were substantially falsified.

Differences below are CE(A)−CE(B), in nats. Ratios divide mean CEs. `analyze.py` computes paired-seed differences, unadjusted Student-t 95% intervals and seed wins. These intervals describe training-seed uncertainty conditional on a split, not population split uncertainty. Numeric seed pairing does not guarantee identical random draws across architectures.

## Primary Measurements

Cell order: d2 plain-first, plain-terminal, residual-first, residual-terminal; then the corresponding d4 cells.

| Split | d2 Mean CEs | d4 Mean CEs |
|---|---|---|
| Easy05 | .002029, .001629, .001795, .004663 | .039052, .070858, .030535, .001999 |
| Easy06 | .010297, .001403, .002007, .004354 | .000938, .001045, .000270, .002090 |
| Hard016 | .480710, .486879, .286576, .561548 | .548359, .580646, .108461, .531283 |
| Hard017 | .496001, .518093, .270502, .572170 | .533906, .614905, .207186, .538880 |

On both hard splits, **first-only LN residuals help**. At d2, R/P differences were −.194134/−.225499, ratios .5962/.5454, with intervals [−.22310,−.16517]/[−.27083,−.18017]. At d4, differences were −.439898/−.326720, ratios .1978/.3881, intervals [−.51291,−.36689]/[−.44390,−.20954]. All four comparisons had 10/10 residual seed wins.

**Terminal-only LN reverses the d2 skip effect:** differences +.074669/+.054077, ratios 1.1534/1.1044, intervals [.05474,.09460]/[.02395,.08421], with 0/10 and 1/10 residual wins. At d4, terminal residuals help: differences −.049363/−.076025, ratios .9150/.8764, intervals excluding zero, with 9/10 and 10/10 wins.

**Plain d4 loses to plain d2 on all four hard placement comparisons:** first-LN differences +.067649/+.037905, ratios 1.1407/1.0764; terminal differences +.093766/+.096812, ratios 1.1926/1.1869. All four intervals exclude zero. Thus “hard data favors depth” fails even with equal LN.

Residual d4 beats d2 on both hard splits and placements. First-LN differences were −.178115/−.063316, ratios .3785/.7659; the second interval includes zero. Terminal differences were −.030265/−.033290, ratios .9461/.9418; both intervals exclude zero.

For hard residual models, terminal/first placement ratios were 1.9595/2.1152 at d2 and 4.8984/2.6009 at d4. Terminal LN won 0/10 seeds in every comparison. Placement is a strong conditioning variable, not an identified physical mechanism.

On easy splits, terminal d2 residual/plain ratios were 2.8620/3.1028, differences +.003034/+.002951, intervals excluding zero, and 0/10 residual wins. Easy d4 ratios disagree between splits and are tail-sensitive: Easy05 included valid seed CEs .389064 for plain-first, .493498/.211719 for plain-terminal, and .302411 for residual-first. These poor fits were retained, not classified as failed seeds. Mean depth signs often disagree with seed-majority signs.

Initial prediction success was residual11/16, complexity-based depth7/16 and terminal placement4/16. These counts reuse four splits.

## Prospective Test

At the checkpoint, `refresh_observations` pinned `Jd9b956477b38_research_e0011_v000001_68a0847b0a38`. Checkpoint history/KB were saved separately; original inputs remain preserved.

Before measuring two allowed **2.5-turn splits**, `0158dd/02e7ca`, preregistered predictions were: first-LN residual helps at both depths; terminal residual hurts d2 and helps d4; d4 hurts plain and helps residual; terminal placement hurts every architecture state. Optimizer and all other settings remained unchanged.

| Split | d2 Mean CEs | d4 Mean CEs |
|---|---|---|
| 0158dd | .513082, .565862, .488432, .552765 | .599393, .660426, .427780, .559632 |
| 02e7ca | .545176, .566065, .489048, .573282 | .629095, .662491, .401362, .542310 |

Predictions matched **22/24 mean signs on two new independent splits**: skip7/8, depth7/8, placement8/8.

First-LN d2 R/P ratios were .9520/.8970, differences −.024650/−.056128; the first interval includes zero. First-LN d4 ratios were .7137/.6380, differences −.171613/−.227733, intervals [−.20949,−.13373]/[−.26460,−.19087], with 10/10 wins both.

Two prospective counterexamples limit the terminal rule. On0158dd, terminal d2 residual **helped**: ratio .9769, difference −.013097, interval [−.04239,.01620], 7/10 wins. Terminal residual d4 **lost to d2**: ratio1.0124, difference +.006867, interval [−.01318,.02691], 4/10 wins. Both intervals include zero. On02e7ca the predicted signs held, but their intervals also included zero.

Across all **four hard splits**, first-LN residuals win8/8 fixed-depth mean comparisons: d2 ratios .5454–.9520 and d4 .1978–.7137. First-LN residual d4/d2 wins4/4 means, ratios .3785–.8758, with 3/4 intervals excluding zero. Plain d4/d2 loses8/8 across placements, ratios1.0764–1.1926, with all intervals excluding zero.

Terminal d2 residual loses only3/4 hard means; terminal residual d4/d2 wins only3/4. Each has only2/4 intervals excluding zero. The terminal boundary is weaker, not a proven turn threshold.

The combined d4-residual versus d2-plain shortcut wins all four hard first-LN comparisons, ratios .2256/.4177/.8337/.7362. With terminal LN it wins only2/4, ratios1.0912/1.0401/.9890/.9580. **Equal LN alone cannot rank these architectures.**

## Minimal SiLU Bridge

Because q_07bc60’s winner used SiLU, a preregistered bridge changed only activation at d2, crossing skip and first/terminal placement on the same four primary splits.

SiLU cells, ordered plain-first, plain-terminal, residual-first, residual-terminal:

- Easy05: .002640, .002846, .002547, .004425.
- Easy06: .003480, .002810, .002842, .004260.
- Hard016: .462084, .157804, .039105, .391861.
- Hard017: .497546, .159071, .045278, .381672.

Predicted first-LN residual benefit and terminal residual penalty held on all four split means, **8/8 signs**, not eight independent splits. Easy first-LN benefits remain imprecise. Easy terminal R/P ratios1.5545/1.5160 had differences +.001578/+.001450, intervals excluding zero, and 0/10 residual wins.

Hard SiLU first-LN R/P ratios were .0846/.0910, differences −.422979/−.452268, intervals [−.45360,−.39235]/[−.47898,−.42555], with 10/10 wins. Terminal R/P ratios were2.4832/2.3994, differences +.234057/+.222602, intervals [.18640,.28172]/[.17246,.27274], with 0/10 wins.

However, **plain terminal LN now helps on both hard splits**, terminal/first ratios .3415/.3197, whereas residual terminal LN hurts, ratios10.0208/8.4295. The ReLU placement preference does not transfer independently of activation. No d4-SiLU or width256 transfer was measured.

## Mechanisms, Accounting And Limits

Terminal preLN normalizes **branch input only**, not the residual stream or head input. No supported scale hooks, stream/head normalization intervention or scalar-tail intervention were identified or executed. Existing loss curves are not feature/gradient instrumentation. Endpoints cannot identify radius retention, head conditioning or branch-versus-stream scale.

Competing explanations include optimization stability and tail failures, effective nonlinear capacity, feature geometry and residual accumulation. Their endpoint predictions overlap. Discriminating them requires supported feature/gradient measurements or stream/head interventions.

There were **64 unique cells and640 seed evaluations**:48 ReLU cells on six independent splits and16 SiLU cells reusing four primary splits. Zero reported failures/exclusions. Eight subsequent cached manifest retrievals were reuse, not replications. All192 measurement artifacts passed SHA-256 verification. `results/*.json`, `analyze.py`, `contrasts.json`, preregistered variants and `report.md` preserve provenance and analysis.

An input inspection raised a missing-field KeyError; one experiment request rejected unsupported metadata before training. Two longer KB drafts failed the claim-length gate. These failures altered no measurements. Scoped claim **K1152** and a K1020 annotation were submitted; no cluster merge/deletion was performed.

The predictive boundary is conditional on **optimizer, activation, LN placement, skip status and depth**. Strong hard first-LN signs survived two prospective splits; terminal signs weakened or failed. Easy means remain tail-sensitive. No export is justified to low-rate AdamW, RMSprop, more-LN, Leaky .01, other widths, longer budgets, original full rankings or arbitrary turn thresholds.

A further distinguishable prediction, **not executed**, is the same frozen ReLU regime on allowed three-turn splits0717d7/0cfa0b: first-LN d4R < d2R < d2P < d4P. No terminal-d2 sign prediction is made. Test both independent split means and paired-seed uncertainty. Scale instrumentation and wider/deeper smooth-model transfer remain unresolved.
